narr: The remnants of TS Debby tracked through St. Lawrence County during the afternoon/early evening of August 9, 2024. This produced a 50-75 mile swath of excessive rainfall from 3 to 7 inches which led to widespread flash flooding. Subsequent information indicated over 100 roads damaged or washed out with several bridges damaged and/or destroyed. Some flood damage to homes also occurred in a few locations along with several swift water rescues.
ev: Emergency Mgmt. and Dept. of Highways reported numerous roads closed or damaged due to flash flooding in the towns of Gouverneur, Fowler, Edwards and Hermon. This included, but was not limited to Route 58.

Tribal Emergency Mgmt. reported flash flooding in and around Hogansburg, NY due to excessive rainfall. Numerous other locations of flash flooding were observed in the towns of Bombay, Helena and Ft. Covington. Locations included, but were not limited to NY State Route 37 and Beaver Meadow Rd.

Emergency Mgmt. reported widespread flash flooding across the area with numerous roads closed or washed out due to severe flash flooding. This included, but was not limited to US Route 11 in numerous locations. Some homes and bridges were also damaged with a few swift water rescues noted. The hardest hit areas were around Canton, Colton, Potsdam and Stockholm.
